name: toyota_a25a_fks
source:
PHYS-033 P4 I7a C7, review round 1 fixes B1/B2/B3/F1/F2/F3 (out/c7/build_map3.py in the physics_sim worktree, reproducible, not committed). 2018 Toyota 2.5L A25A-FKS 'Dynamic Force' Atkinson-cycle I4 (2018 Toyota Camry LE). Two SEPARATE source documents (F3, not conflated): (a) EPA NVFEL Fuel Analysis Report 26781, '2018 Toyota 2.5L A25A-FKS Engine Tier 3 Fuel - Test Data Package', Version 2020-07 (Ann Arbor, MI: US EPA, National Center for Advanced Technology, 2020); (b) the accompanying Test Data Package xlsx workbook '4- 2018 Toyota 2.5L A25A-FKS Engine Tier 3 Fuel - Test Data.xlsx'. Cross-referenced against SAE 2019-01-0249 (Kargul et al., 'Benchmarking a 2018 Toyota Camry 2.5-Liter Atkinson Cycle Engine with Cooled-EGR'), Table 1: rated power 151 kW @ 6600 rpm, rated torque 249 N*m @ 4800 rpm, geometric CR 13:1 - these are Toyota's own published ratings AS CITED in SAE's Table 1, not measurements taken from this test cell (F3): the highest measured point in the xlsx is 5761 rpm and the test cell's own safety limit (Report 26781 Table 5) is 6500 rpm, so no test-cell data exists at or near 6600 rpm.

B1 FIX - WOT envelope rebuilt as each measured speed line's MAXIMUM measured brake torque over ANY pedal position (not just pedal==100), labelled DERIVED 'max over all measured rows on that speed line, from the Steady State + High Load Final sheets (High Load Initial excluded: transient, pre-stabilization, matching this review's own evaluation methodology)': (1003.0,159.04)[HF row8,pedal80] (1153.2,176.65)[HF row11,pedal100] (1325.9,179.95)[HF row14,pedal70] (1498.5,189.62)[HF row17,pedal70] (1728.6,196.62)[HF row20,pedal100] (2017.1,216.32)[HF row23,pedal100] (2534.9,225.13)[HF row26,pedal100] (2995.6,217.81)[HF row29,pedal100] (3571.2,228.40)[HF row32,pedal100] (4032.2,228.35)[HF row34,pedal100] (4493.1,232.04)[HF row37,pedal100] (4954.0,231.44)[HF row39,pedal80 - no pedal100 row exists at this speed line] (5414.5,229.40)[HF row42,pedal100] (5761.2,227.31)[HF row45,pedal80 - CHANGED from the pre-review file's 226.24 at pedal100/row44, which review round 1 identified as ECU-enriched, see below]. The 807 rpm speed line's maximum (SS row18, pedal25, T=108.20) is excluded from the WOT curve: it is far below what a WOT sweep at that speed would read (the 807 rpm line has no High Load rows at all), so including it would badly understate low-speed WOT; m(807) is used instead for the fuel map's rpm axis (F1).

MEASURED EXPLANATION FOR THE ANOMALY (B1, replacing the pre-review file's 'root cause not determined'): at 1326 and 1498 rpm, the High Load Final sheet's pedal-80/100 rows record LOWER torque than the pedal-70 row at the same speed line (1498 rpm: pedal70=189.62 vs pedal100=174.55 N*m; 1326 rpm: pedal70=179.95 vs pedal100=172.94 N*m). This is measured ECU protection-mode fuel enrichment, not a data or column-mapping error: the pedal-80/100 rows there run lambda 0.63-0.73 (e.g. 1498 rpm pedal100 lambda=0.63, 1326 rpm pedal100 lambda=0.73) while MAP is 97.2 kPa (full air induction) in both modes and spark timing is similar (-3.6 to -4.0 deg at 1498 across the sweep) - the ECU is commanding extra fuel at essentially constant air/spark, which only enrichment does. Report 26781's own text states that at this operating region the engine's control strategy is used to 'avoid preignition at low speed/high load' (quoted from the report), i.e. a deliberate protection-mode enrichment that reduces combustion temperature at the cost of torque and efficiency (lambda 0.63-0.73 both means excess unburned fuel AND, per the WOT envelope above, LESS torque than the leaner pedal-70 row at the same speed line - the fuel is not converted to extra work). This project's engine model does NOT reproduce this ECU behavior: the WOT curve here is the physical upper envelope of measured torque (the review's stated fix), and the fuel map (B2/B3 below) excludes the enriched rows from its fit, so a full-throttle command in this engine model draws the LEANER, HIGHER-TORQUE fuel rate a non-protection-limited ECU calibration would use at 1326-1498 rpm - the real vehicle's low-speed WOT torque limitation from this protection strategy is explicitly NOT modelled.

B2 FIX - fuel-map fit uses PARETO-DOMINANCE filtering per speed line, not a hand-picked lambda threshold: on each of the 15 measured speed lines, a fired row (Accelerator Pedal > 0, Fuel Meter Flow present) is DROPPED from that line's Willians-line fit iff another row on the SAME line has torque >= it AND strictly less fuel (i.e. it is dominated - never a better choice for the map, regardless of why). 26 rows dropped in total (xlsx row, rpm, T, fuel_g_s, pedal, lambda): rpm~807.1: none; rpm~1153.0: [HF row10 1153.2 173.28Nm 1.9387g/s pedal60 lambda0.782]; rpm~1326.0: [HF row12 1326.2 171.95Nm 2.4671g/s pedal80 lambda0.735][HF row13 1326.2 172.94Nm 2.4647g/s pedal100 lambda0.732][SS row51 1326.0 171.50Nm 1.7480g/s pedal85 lambda1.000][SS row52 1326.0 172.50Nm 1.7460g/s pedal90 lambda1.010][SS row53 1326.0 172.60Nm 1.7580g/s pedal95 lambda1.000]; rpm~1498.8: [HF row15 1498.8 173.67Nm 3.2946g/s pedal80 lambda0.635][HF row16 1498.7 174.55Nm 3.2877g/s pedal100 lambda0.632][SS row66 1499.0 174.80Nm 1.9930g/s pedal45 lambda1.000]; rpm~1728.9: [HF row18 1728.9 193.53Nm 3.8649g/s pedal80 lambda0.672][SS row80 1729.0 176.90Nm 2.3030g/s pedal45 lambda1.010]; rpm~2017.0: [SS row93 2017.0 183.90Nm 2.6980g/s pedal45 lambda1.000]; rpm~2535.0: [SS row105 2535.0 150.90Nm 2.4700g/s pedal40 lambda1.000][SS row108 2535.0 196.30Nm 3.5390g/s pedal55 lambda1.000]; rpm~2995.9: [HF row27 2995.6 213.03Nm 4.8921g/s pedal70 lambda0.867][SS row121 2996.0 196.30Nm 4.0510g/s pedal55 lambda1.000][SS row122 2996.0 196.70Nm 4.0610g/s pedal60 lambda1.000]; rpm~4493.1: [HF row35 4493.1 230.13Nm 8.2219g/s pedal70 lambda0.854]; rpm~4954.0: [HF row38 4953.8 230.66Nm 9.1048g/s pedal70 lambda0.859]; rpm~5414.5: [HF row41 5414.6 228.19Nm 9.9969g/s pedal80 lambda0.862]; rpm~5761.0: [HF row44 5761.0 226.24Nm 10.9407g/s pedal100 lambda0.829]. Cross-check against a simple lambda>=0.85 filter: the two filters disagree on 12/15 lines; wherever they differ, Pareto is the STRICTER filter (drops a handful of additional lambda~1.00 rows too, e.g. SS rows 37-40 at 1153 rpm) - those extra drops are rows dominated by a nearby better-BSFC point on the same line as the pedal is stepped in small increments (ordinary steady-state measurement scatter), not ECU enrichment; they are excluded because a dominated point is never the right choice for a monotonic Willans-line fit, not because they are suspected of enrichment. Below the lowest Pareto-kept fired point on a line, B3 (below) interpolates rather than extrapolates. Above the highest kept point, the fit still linearly extrapolates the top two kept points (unchanged from the pre-review methodology).

B3 FIX - below the lowest Pareto-kept fired point on each speed line, fuel is interpolated LINEARLY (not extrapolated) between the measured zero-fuel motoring point (T=m(rpm), fuel=0 g/s, DERIVED from this file's own motoring curve) and that lowest kept fired point - replacing the pre-review file's linear EXTRAPOLATION of the two lowest fired points, which at 4493 rpm/theta=0.02 drove the Willans line through zero fuel at tau_comb=+1.7 N*m instead of <=0 like every other speed line, understating fuel there by about 31% and inflating the apparent indicated efficiency to a physically implausible 61.92%. With the fix, the map's new maximum indicated indicated efficiency (sampled at every map node, cell midpoint, row-mid and column-mid, and every WOT/motoring breakpoint crossed with every load node) is 45.96% at rpm=2017.0, theta=0.600 (next-highest: 45.87% at 2996.0/0.700, 45.82% at 2996.0/0.650, 45.78% at 2017.0/0.550, 45.77% at 2765.5/0.700) - a plausible spread, well clear of 100%, with no single-point extrapolation artefact.

F1 FIX - fuel-map rpm axis extended to the full set of measured speed lines 807/1003/1153/1326/1498/1728/2017/2535/2996/3571/4032/4493/4954/5414/5761 (the pre-review file covered only 1326-4954; 807/1003/1153/5414/5761 are measured lines the old map clamped, with clamp errors up to +58 to +98% at 1003 rpm and -15 to -17% at 5761 rpm WOT) plus a DERIVED 6600 rpm row, built by linear EXTRAPOLATION in rpm of the last two measured lines (5414/5761) AT EACH LOAD COLUMN independently (not a single global slope) - e.g. at theta=1.0: (10.8121-9.9861)/(5761.0-5414.0)=2.386 g/s per 1000rpm, extrapolated to 6600 gives 12.8093 g/s. m(rpm) at the newly-added 807/1003/1153/5414/5761 rows comes from this file's own motoring_torque_nm_vs_rpm Curve1D (DERIVED, zero new data). WOT torque at those rows likewise comes from this file's own wot_torque_nm_vs_rpm curve. DERIVED motoring_torque_nm_vs_rpm 6600 knot: linear extension of the last two measured knots (4493,-37.40)-(4954,-42.30), slope=-0.010629 N*m/rpm, m(6600)=-59.80 N*m; below 1326 rpm the existing linear extrapolation to y(0)=-17.5 N*m is unchanged (the same declining trend reasonably covers 807-1153 rpm too; no new motoring knots were added there since the existing two-point extrapolation already spans that range). DERIVED wot_torque_nm_vs_rpm 6600 knot: linear extension of the corrected last two WOT knots (5414.5,229.40)-(5761.2,227.31), slope=-0.006028 N*m/rpm, w(6600)=222.25 N*m = 153.61 kW. Cross-check ONLY (not the source of this knot, F1): Toyota's rated 151 kW @ 6600 rpm (SAE Table 1) implies T=218.48 N*m at 6600 - the DERIVED knot (222.25 N*m / 153.6 kW) is about 1.7% above the cited rated power, plausible since 'rated power' typically reflects a certification/marketing figure rather than the exact peak of a raw dyno sweep's linear extrapolation. Measured-cross-check WOT brake thermal efficiency at the new 6600 rpm knot: fuel(6600,theta=1)=12.8093 g/s, brake power=153.6 kW, fuel power=537.4 kW, BTE=28.6%, safely under the cited peak 39.8% (Tier 2 fuel; SAE 2019-01-0249 notes a minor BTE drop with Tier 3 fuel but gives no explicit Tier-3 peak) - reported as measured, not tuned to stay under any bound. Below the lowest WOT knot (1003.0 rpm), the curve's flat hold down to 0 rpm is Curve1D's own clamped-edge behavior; this hold is ASSUMED (F1, relabelled from implicit in the pre-review file - no measured or published data exists below 1003 rpm for WOT).

F2 FIX - limiter.rpm = 6600 is relabelled ASSUMED (was 'CITED...honest' in the pre-review file). It is Toyota's rated-POWER engine speed (SAE 2019-01-0249 Table 1), not a measured or published fuel-cut speed; it is also above both the test cell's own 6500 rpm safety limit (Report 26781 Table 5) and the highest rpm actually measured in the xlsx (5761 rpm). No citable fuel-cut rpm exists for this engine in the reviewed sources, so 6600 is kept only as a plausible round-number placeholder tied to the one real rpm fact available (rated power speed), and is explicitly an assumption, not a citation.

F3 FIX (engine-file half; see data/fuels/tier3_e10_cert.json's own source field for the fuel-file half): the pre-review file's citation 'Fuel Analysis Report 26781 / Test Data Package' improperly conflated two separate documents - split above into (a) Report 26781 itself and (b) the accompanying xlsx Test Data Package workbook. The rated 151 kW / 249 N*m figures quoted in this file are Toyota's OWN ratings as CITED in SAE 2019-01-0249's Table 1 - they are not measurements taken by EPA NVFEL in this test cell (the highest measured points are 5761 rpm / 232.04 N*m peak, both below the respective rated figures' operating points of 6600/4800 rpm).

KNOWN DATA ANOMALY (unchanged from pre-review, still not corrected/used, now understood per B1 above): the same 'High Load Initial' transient sheet shows the same pedal-70-beats-pedal-100 pattern at 1326/1498 rpm; excluded from both the WOT envelope and the fuel-map fit (transient, pre-stabilization, per this review's own methodology, matching SAE 2019-01-0249's description of the High Load Initial sweep).

ASSUMED (no citable value found in the reviewed report/paper/xlsx 'Test Parameter List' sheet; copied from data/engines/i4_2l_na.json, a plausible-class placeholder, and labeled here as an assumption per PHYS-033 P4 I7a C7 rules): inertia_kgm2, breakaway_torque_nm, idle_rpm, stall_rpm, fire_rpm, start_complete_rpm, dfco_enable_rpm, dfco_reenable_rpm, idle_control, starter, crank_axis_local, initial_state.

fuel_map.source: PHYS-033 P4 I7a C7, review round 1 fixes B1/B2/B3/F1 (out/c7/build_map3.py in the physics_sim worktree, reproducible, not committed - stdlib xlsx parse of the same xlsx as wot_torque_nm_vs_rpm/motoring_torque_nm_vs_rpm above). rpm axis = the 15 measured speed lines (807/1003/1153/1326/1498/1728/2017/2535/2996/3571/4032/4493/4954/5414/5761, F1 extends this from the pre-review file's 1326-4954 subset) plus a DERIVED 6600 row (F1: linear rpm-extrapolation of the 5414/5761 rows, per load column independently). load axis = theta_c, dense near 0 per PHYS-033 P4 I7a C7's instruction. DERIVED for every (rpm,load) node with load>0 and rpm<=5761: target torque T = m(rpm) + load*(w(rpm)-m(rpm)) using this file's own motoring/WOT Curve1D knots; fuel flow at that T is read off a per-speed-line piecewise-linear Willans fit through the PARETO-DOMINANCE-FILTERED fired points on that line (B2: a fired row is dropped from the fit iff another row on the same line has torque >= it and strictly less fuel - 26 rows dropped in total, see the engine file's own source field for the full cited list and the B2/B3 methodology). Below the lowest Pareto-kept fired point, fuel is interpolated LINEARLY between the measured zero-fuel motoring point (T=m(rpm), fuel=0) and that lowest kept point (B3 fix - replaces the pre-review file's extrapolation of the two lowest fired points, which produced an implausible 61.92% max indicated efficiency artifact at 4493 rpm/theta=0.02; the new max is 45.96% at rpm=2017.0, theta=0.600, see the engine file's own source field). Above the highest kept fired point, fuel is still linearly extrapolated from the top two kept points (unchanged). The rpm=6600 row is NOT built this way: it is a per-load-column linear rpm-extrapolation of the 5414/5761 rows (F1), since no fired data exists above 5761 rpm. load==0 column forced to exactly 0.0 (format requirement, docs/data_formats/engine.md). Error stats (against every measured FIRED row in the map's rpm range, the review's own instruction, xlsx literals, rows cited in evalmap-style output captured in build_map3.py's own console log): BEFORE this fix (old WOT/motoring/map, rows in [1326,4954]): n=133, max=66.33% (rpm=1499.0, T=176.30, SS row 67, theta=1.000, lambda=1.010), median=0.40%, >5%: 17, >10%: 12. AFTER this fix, full range [807,6600]: n=182, max=41.10% (rpm=1498.8, T=173.67, HF row 15, theta=0.925, lambda=0.635 - a Pareto-dropped, ECU-enriched row: comparing the map against its OWN excluded row is expected to show a large gap, since the map was deliberately NOT fit to it), median=0.50%, >5%: 23, >10%: 11; old-comparable range [1326,4954]: n=133, same max/median, >5%: 14, >10%: 5. The load-time >100% thermal-efficiency check (docs/data_formats/engine.md's sampled rule) was run against this exact table and this file's LHV (41954062 J/kg, data/fuels/tier3_e10_cert.json) and PASSED with margin - maximum observed indicated efficiency 45.96% at rpm=2017, theta=0.6, a plausible spread (see the engine file's own source field for the full top-5 and the B3 fix that removed the old 61.92% extrapolation artifact); no node required adjustment.
